  <section class="home-section research-front" data-reveal aria-labelledby="research-front-title">
    <header class="section-heading section-heading-wide">
      <p>RESEARCH PROGRAM</p>
      <h2 id="research-front-title">From forecasts to operators, with decisions as the test.</h2>
      <p>My doctoral work linked forecasting, uncertainty representation, and constrained optimization in coupled water–energy systems. I extend the same principle to neural operators: learn distributed physical dynamics, then evaluate the model through the control action, feasible design, or operating decision it changes.</p>
    </header>
    <div class="research-program-grid">
      <article class="research-thread theme-decision">
        <p class="thread-stage">Doctoral foundation</p>
        <h3>Decision-focused forecasting</h3>
        <p>Probabilistic predictions are trained and evaluated through the schedules, costs, and constraints they induce in coupled water–energy systems.</p>
      </article>
      <article class="research-thread theme-operator">
        <p class="thread-stage">Method extension</p>
        <h3>Neural operators for distributed dynamics</h3>
        <p>I study function-to-function models that map initial conditions, geometry, boundary conditions, and forcing terms to spatiotemporal solution fields.</p>
      </article>
      <article class="research-thread theme-physical">
        <p class="thread-stage">Decision criterion</p>
        <h3>Operator-based control and optimization</h3>
        <p>I examine how rollout error, gradient error, and constraint violation alter closed-loop actions and optimized designs.</p>
      </article>
      <article class="research-thread theme-materials">
        <p class="thread-stage">Physical testbed</p>
        <h3>Materials processes</h3>
        <p>Field-evolving materials processes provide a concrete setting for experiment selection, process control, and constrained design with learned solution maps.</p>
      </article>
    </div>
    <p class="section-link"><a href="/research/">Methods and research questions</a></p>
  </section>

      <p>These papers established the criterion I carry into operator learning: evaluate prediction through the timing, cost, feasibility, and physical action it changes.</p>

        <div class="paper-body"><p class="paper-meta"><span class="author-role">FIRST AUTHOR</span><span>IEEE TSG · 2025</span></p><h3><a href="https://doi.org/10.1109/TSG.2025.3601238">End-to-End Stochastic Predict-Then-Optimize for Cost-Efficient Water-Energy Resource Scheduling</a></h3><p class="paper-authors"><strong class="author-self">Shunyu Wu</strong>, Jingcheng Wang, Haotian Xu, Yanjiu Zhong, and Jun Rao</p><p class="paper-claim">SPTO trains a probabilistic forecast with a differentiable upper bound on downstream optimality gap, placing scheduling cost inside the learning objective.</p></div>

        <div class="paper-body"><p class="paper-meta"><span class="author-role">FIRST AUTHOR</span><span>ESWA · 2024</span></p><h3><a href="https://doi.org/10.1016/j.eswa.2024.124508">Knowledge-based Bi-correction model for lag-free urban water-demand forecasting</a></h3><p class="paper-authors"><strong class="author-self">Shunyu Wu</strong>, Jingcheng Wang, Haotian Xu, Shangwei Zhao, and Jiahui Xu</p><p class="paper-claim">Lag-penalty attention and posterior residual correction target delayed reactions near demand turning points.</p></div>
      </article>
      <article class="paper-card">

        <div class="paper-body"><p class="paper-meta"><span class="author-role">FIRST AUTHOR</span><span>IEEE TCSS · 2024</span></p><h3><a href="https://doi.org/10.1109/TCSS.2023.3272330">CritiCoder: Uncertain regression for robust pressure models</a></h3><p class="paper-authors"><strong class="author-self">Shunyu Wu</strong>, Jingcheng Wang, Haotian Xu, Shangwei Zhao, and Jiahui Xu</p><p class="paper-claim">The Coder learns measured effects, while the Critic represents residual pressure variation associated with unobserved disturbances.</p></div>
      </article>

      </article>
